title: Norway May Still Get to Play at the World Juniors
summary: Norway's young hockey players might still play at the world junior championships after all. The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said on Sunday that Norway is being moved out of the tournament so Russia can take part instead. The change follows a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which let Russian teams return to international play. The tournament for the best male players under 20 starts on December 26 in Alberta, Canada. But the hockey federation has not formally announced the change, and its website still lists Norway. Norway, ranked tenth, would drop to the 1A Division. Russia may not get to play either: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has said he will not let the Russian team enter Canada, which could open the door for Norway again. "The situation is still unclear," said Peter Salsten, Norway's ice hockey secretary general. Six nations, including Norway, have promised not to play Russia while the war in Ukraine goes on. Some sponsors have also said they will pull out if Russia plays. Russia has not played in the tournament since 2021.
why_it_matters: If you play a team sport, this story shows how rules and fair play matter even for the best young players in the world.
